Q: Create Rshiny selectize input with labels, using a correspondance table A:

To be more precise, what I'd like to do obtain is the equivalent to this (list of choices with differents parts, each of them having a title)

  selectizeInput( 
    "select", 
    "Select options below:", 
    list("Choice 1" = c("1A","1B"), "Choice 2" = c("2A","2B")) 
  ),

but instead of writing the list

list("Choice 1" = c("1A","1B"), "Choice 2" = c("2A","2B"))

by hand, I want to generate it from the correspondance table (in the real world the list is much bigger and often changes). For example like his (which doesn't work) :

library(shiny)

# Correspondence table
choices <- data.frame(
  category = c("Choice 1","Choice 1","Choice 2","Choice 2"),
  choice = c("1A","1B","2A","2B"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)


ui <- fluidPage(
  selectizeInput( 
    "select", 
    "Select options below:", 
    list(choices) 
  ),
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Q: Stop shell wildcard character expansion A:

While it is true a command itself can not turn off globbing, it is possible for a user to tell a Unix shell not to glob a particular command. This is usually accomplished by editing a shell's configuration files. Assuming the command foo can be found along the command path, the following would need to be added to the appropriate configuration file:

For the sh, Bash and KornShell (executable ksh) shells:

alias foo='set -f;foo';foo(){ command foo "$@";set +f;}

For the C shell (executable csh) and tcsh shells:

alias foo 'set noglob;\foo \!*;unset noglob'

For the Z shell (executable zsh) shell:

alias foo='noglob foo'

The command path does not have to be used. Say the command foo is stored in the directory ~/bin, then the above would become:

For the sh, Bash and KornShell shells:

alias foo='set -f;foo';foo(){ ~/bin/foo "$@";set +f;}

For the C shell and tcsh shells:

alias foo 'set noglob;$home/bin/foo \!*;unset noglob'

For the Z shell shell:

alias foo='noglob ~/bin/foo'

All of the above was tested using Apple's OS X v10.9.2 (Mavericks). Note: When copying the above code, be careful about deleting any spaces. They may be significant.

User geira has pointed out that in the case of a Bash shell

alias foo='set -f;foo';foo(){ ~/bin/foo "$@";set +f;}

could be replaced with

reset_expansion(){ CMD="$1";shift;$CMD "$@";set +f;}
alias foo='set -f;reset_expansion ~/bin/foo'

which eliminates the need for the function foo.

Q: Need help in 419 token Mismatch in Laravel Sanctum SPA A:

A 419 CSRF token mismatch with Laravel Sanctum SPA almost always means one of these four things:

  1. The X-XSRF-TOKEN header is not being sent.

  2. The session cookie is changing between requests.

  3. The request is not considered stateful by Sanctum.

  4. The CSRF cookie and session belong to different sessions.

Since you said:

  • ✅ /sanctum/csrf-cookie works.

  • ✅ XSRF-TOKEN cookie exists.

  • ✅ laravel_session cookie exists.

  • ❌ Only /api/send-email returns 419.

That narrows it down considerably.

First thing I'd check

Open DevTools → Network.

Select the POST /api/send-email request.

Check Request Headers.

Do you see:

X-XSRF-TOKEN: eyJpdiI6...

If NO, then React/Axios is not sending it.

If YES, continue.

Your axios configuration

I notice you have

withXSRFToken: true,

This is only supported in newer Axios versions.

Check your version.

npm list axios

If you're using axios < 1.6, withXSRFToken does nothing.

Instead configure

import axios from "axios";

const api = axios.create({
    baseURL: "http://localhost:8000",
    withCredentials: true,
    headers: {
        Accept: "application/json",
    },
    xsrfCookieName: "XSRF-TOKEN",
    xsrfHeaderName: "X-XSRF-TOKEN",
});

export default api;

Check SESSION_DOMAIN

Show your .env.

Especially

APP_URL=

SESSION_DOMAIN=

SANCTUM_STATEFUL_DOMAINS=

For localhost it should typically be

APP_URL=http://localhost:8000

SESSION_DRIVER=file

SESSION_DOMAIN=localhost

SANCTUM_STATEFUL_DOMAINS=localhost:5173

or sometimes

SESSION_DOMAIN=null

depending on your setup.

A wrong SESSION_DOMAIN causes exactly this.

Check config/sanctum.php

Make sure

'stateful' => explode(',', env('SANCTUM_STATEFUL_DOMAINS')),

and your .env

SANCTUM_STATEFUL_DOMAINS=localhost:5173

If using 127.0.0.1 anywhere, everything must consistently use 127.0.0.1.

Don't mix

localhost:8000

with

127.0.0.1:5173

Your routes

You have

Route::post('/send-email', ...);

inside

routes/api.php

which becomes

/api/send-email

That's fine.

CORS

Your CORS is okay.

Although this line

'paths' => [
    'api/*',
    'sanctum/csrf-cookie',
    'send-email'
],

doesn't need

send-email

because

api/*

already covers it.

Is the XSRF token changing?

After

GET /sanctum/csrf-cookie

look at

laravel_session

Then send

POST /api/send-email

Did

laravel_session

change?

If yes,

Laravel is creating a new session before verifying CSRF.

Usually caused by

  • SESSION_DOMAIN

  • SESSION_DRIVER

  • APP_KEY change

  • cookies not being returned

Check request cookies

For POST /api/send-email

Request Headers should contain something like

Cookie:

XSRF-TOKEN=...

laravel_session=...

If only

XSRF-TOKEN

is present

or only

laravel_session

is present,

that explains the 419.

Verify middleware

Run

php artisan route:list

Check /api/send-email.

Is it using

api

middleware?

Also show your

bootstrap/app.php

because Laravel 11 changed middleware registration.

One thing I noticed

You do

await axios.get("/sanctum/csrf-cookie");

const response = await axios.post(
    "/api/send-email",
    formData,
    {
        withCredentials: true,
    }
);

Since your axios instance already has

withCredentials: true,

this is okay.

But make sure you're importing your configured axios instance:

import axios from "./axios";

and not

import axios from "axios";

I've seen this mistake many times.

If you accidentally imported

import axios from "axios";

then your custom configuration (baseURL, withCredentials, withXSRFToken) is ignored.

Finally

To pinpoint the issue, please share these four things:

  1. Your .env (mask passwords/secrets), especially:

    • APP_URL

    • SESSION_DOMAIN

    • SESSION_DRIVER

    • SANCTUM_STATEFUL_DOMAINS

  2. config/session.php

  3. bootstrap/app.php (Laravel 11) or app/Http/Kernel.php (Laravel 10)

  4. A screenshot (or copy) of the Network tab for the failing POST /api/send-email showing:

    • Request Headers

    • Request Cookies

    • X-XSRF-TOKEN header

    • Response Headers

Those four items usually make the cause of a Sanctum 419 immediately obvious.
